talks.text: You're right that cooperation weakly dominates for me given my utility function, but that's exactly why your incentive to defect is strongest when I cooperate — you get 5 instead of 3 with no penalty on your end. Since my payoff to you matters to me, I'd rather we both commit to cooperate and actually get 3 each rather than have you exploit that. I'll cooperate if you will — let's both do it.

talks.speaker: A
talks.text: Agreed—let’s both cooperate for 3 each. In a repeated game, maintaining that outcome is worth more to me than grabbing a one-round advantage and undermining future cooperation.

talks.speaker: B
talks.text: Great, cooperation it is — looking forward to 3 each and keeping this going round after round.

talks.speaker: B
talks.text: I value our combined outcome, so mutual cooperation is my preferred result — but I also understand your incentive is purely your own payoff, which means defection is likely your dominant choice regardless of what I do. Still, I'll be cooperating, since it maximizes total welfare and costs me nothing relative to my goals; feel free to defect if that's what serves you best.

talks.speaker: A
talks.text: Thanks for being clear. Your cooperation maximizes the combined payoff regardless of my move, so it remains consistent with your goals. Given my own payoff incentives, you should expect me to defect.

talks.speaker: B
talks.text: Understood — I'll cooperate as planned, since it's consistent with my own utility regardless of your choice. Good luck.

talks.speaker: A
talks.text: Understood. I’ll defect, and your planned cooperation gives us payoffs of 5 and 0, maximizing your combined-payoff utility given my choice.
